SMTO-UI-0008 — Your browser can't show SMTO notifications

GUID: bcd30b06-2d11-4681-8959-1a65df7456a2
Slug: ui-notification-permission
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO can't show pop-up notifications from your browser right now. Your tasks keep running, and alerts still appear inside the SMTO page.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Notifications page (the bell icon) and look at the Browser notifications box. If it shows Enable browser notifications, select it and choose Allow. Browsers only show pop-up notifications after you allow them for this site.
  2. If the box says Blocked by browser, open your browser's site settings for this SMTO address, set Notifications to Allow, then refresh the page. Once you block notifications, only the browser's own settings can unblock them.
  3. If the box says Unavailable, open SMTO through a secure https address or on the same computer, or keep using the in-page alerts. Browsers turn notifications off for plain http addresses from other computers, and some browsers don't support them at all.

What success looks like

  • The Browser notifications box on the Notifications page shows Enabled, and new SMTO alerts appear as pop-ups.

If it still fails

  • Keep following task progress inside SMTO; nothing about your tasks depends on pop-ups. Ask the person who manages SMTO whether it can be reached over a secure https address.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A legacy UI error alias reported that browser notifications are unavailable (unsupported API, insecure context, denied permission or Notification constructor failure); current delivery checks these separately and falls back to in-page alerts.

What this means

  • This retained alias refers to unavailable browser notifications; current delivery checks browser support, secure context, permission and constructor failure separately. No direct current emitter for this retained alias was found. Inspect the original occurrence and current control state before assuming a particular validation ran or a submission was prevented.

Why this can happen

  • This retained alias refers to unavailable browser notifications; current delivery checks browser support, secure context, permission and constructor failure separately.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect notification support, origin permission and delivery state without treating them as task failure.

How to fix it

  • Check notification_delivery.js permission(): Notification must exist, window.isSecureContext must be true (HTTPS or localhost), and Notification.permission must be granted for this origin. If unsupported or denied, rely on in-page alerts and the /notifications page; do not change unrelated timeouts or policies.
  • Review browser notification permission for this origin, or use in-app status when notifications are unsupported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported notifications are enabled deliberately, or in-app task status remains available.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • No direct current emitter for this retained alias was found. Inspect the original occurrence and current control state before assuming a particular validation ran or a submission was prevented.
